title: Hybrid slice handoff scheduler for attention kernel harmonics across H100/L40S/A10
creator: Sofia Chen
description:
Problem: In mixed-SKU MIG clusters (H100/L40S/A10) we observe kernel-selection oscillation and attention kernel handshake failures under transient load, which amplifies tail latency. Frequent small jobs land on slices with insufficient clock headroom or cold KV caches and trigger kernel fallback paths, increasing p99 decode latency by ~30% in our stress tests. Existing heuristics pick kernels per-request and then attempt to pack slices; they lack a coordinated handoff and clock-awareness strategy when requests cross MIG boundaries.

Goal: Build a hybrid 'slice handoff' scheduler that: (1) groups requests by predicted kernel + attention footprint, (2) probes candidate slices with microbatches to warm KV caches and verify clock headroom before commit, (3) tags requests with kernel-hints so runtime performs deterministic kernel selection, and (4) exposes a fallback hedging policy when thermal headroom drops. This should reduce kernel churn, lower p99 latency, and improve sustained throughput for mixed-SKU fleets.

Approach:
- Request classification: lightweight estimator at ingress (using sequence length, model variant, sampling params) to predict a preferred attention kernel and expected KV cache size.
- Candidate selection: score slices by (compatibility, current clock governor headroom, recent failure rate, probe latency). Include heuristics to prefer same-sku slices when the kernel requires specific optimized microkernels.
- Probe-and-commit: issue a 1-token microbatch to the top candidate to warm caches and observe kernel dispatch path and wall-time; only commit the full request if probe passes latency thresholds. Probes are charged as part of batching cost accounting.
- Clock harmonics hints: annotate chosen slices with a 'clock-hint' to the clock governor subsystem so it can avoid aggressive downclock during active handoff windows.
- Hedging policy: if probe fails or headroom disappears mid-request, transparently redirect to a compatible fallback slice (quantized variant or higher-latency kernel) with a configurable hedging budget.

Trade-offs considered:
- Probing adds a small extra token cost and slightly more runtime complexity, but prevents expensive kernel fallbacks later.
- Preferring same-sku slices may marginally decrease aggregate packing efficiency but yields large tail-latency wins for attention-heavy workloads.
- Clock-hints can conflict with global power policies; we gate hints under per-customer SLA tiers and prefer conservative hints for shared tenants.

Success metrics:
- p99 decode latency improvement >= 20% on mixed-sku MIG stress tests (target: 25% at launch).
- 95th percentile downstream kernel fallback count per 10k requests reduced by >= 60%.
- Sustained throughput improvement +10% for long sequences (>=1024 tokens) in mixed fleets.

Testbed & experiments:
- Testbed: 8-node cluster with 2x H100 (MIG split 7g.40), 4x L40S, 2x A10; synthetic workload mix: 60% short-chat (<=128 tokens), 40% long-completion (>=1024 tokens).
- Baseline: current packer + per-request kernel chooser.
- Raw results (avg of 5 runs): p99 decode baseline 184ms -> handoff scheduler 139ms (24% improvement); throughput baseline 1.00x -> 1.12x; kernel fallback rate baseline 7.5/10k -> 2.8/10k.

Implementation plan (phased):
- Phase 1 (spike, 2 weeks): implement estimator + candidate scorer + probe flow in the dev runtime; collect telemetry.
- Phase 2 (integration, 3 weeks): add clock-hint integration with governor agent, hedging policy, and admin controls per-tenant.
- Phase 3 (canary, 2 weeks): rollout to dedicated fleet subset, expose observability (per-request decision trace, probe success rate).
- Phase 4 (gradual rollout): expand to all mixed-sku clusters behind rollout policy; iterate on scorer weights.

Open questions:
- Probe cost accounting: bill the request owner or amortize across the batch? (Currently billing owner; finance asked for a simpler amortization model for low-value micro-probes.)
- How to choose conservative clock-hint thresholds to avoid cross-tenant SLA violation.

Next steps:
1) Merge design doc and get eng+infra signoff (target 2026-02-24).
2) Spike implementation branch and synthetic test harness (PR created).
3) Run extended soak for 48h on staging MIG fleet and collect telemetry.
acceptance_criteria: Scheduler routes >=95% of long-sequence requests to probed candidate slices when available.
p99 decode latency in mixed-sku MIG testbed improves >=20% compared to baseline.
Probe failure rate <2% and hedging success rate >=95% when probes fail.
Clock-hint mechanism has opt-out per-tenant and does not increase overall power budget beyond agreed SLA.
Observability: per-request decision trace and probe metrics show up in Grafana dashboards.
